claims.text: High-precision DSC analysis can determine melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, and fusion entropy accurately and efficiently across the high-entropy-alloy family.
Adding in situ dilatometry to DSC can determine the volume change at melting.
The combined method can determine liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across the high-entropy-alloy family.
Rapid heating near the solidus minimizes thermal lag while retaining measurable resolution of the heat-capacity anomaly.
Dulong-Petit baseline assumptions describe low-temperature heat-capacity behavior.
The method is most applicable to HEAs without complicating solid-solid phase transitions near melting.
Configurational entropy governs the baseline heat capacity of the alloy.
Temperature-dependent lattice vibrations produce a Dulong-Petit heat-capacity baseline at sufficiently high solid-state temperatures.
Heat capacity rises sharply when the solidus temperature is reached.
The sharp heat-capacity rise near the solidus enables detection of latent heat and calculation of fusion enthalpy and entropy.
At low temperature, solid-state heat capacity follows the Debye T^3 law.
Near room temperature, heat capacity approaches the Dulong-Petit value of 3R when no magnetic or phase transformation intervenes.
Integrating the heat-capacity curve provides the baseline thermal-entropy contribution.
Latent heat can be isolated from a discontinuous jump in the DSC signal.
Simultaneous thermal-expansion measurement maps the volume change associated with melting.
Lever-rule-inspired partitioning separates gradual heat-capacity contributions from the latent-heat event.
The method will measure melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, and fusion entropy to approximately ±5% relative to benchmark alloys.
Overlapping solid-state transformations or decomposition before melting can make interpretation difficult.

The approach is ruled out if fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and volume change differ from independent measurements by more than ±5–10% for multiple HEA compositions, or if no distinct latent-heat signal can be resolved.

contradictions.description: The intervention invokes Dulong-Petit assumptions for low-temperature behavior, whereas the mechanism assigns low-temperature behavior to the Debye T^3 law and places the Dulong-Petit plateau near room temperature or above.
